# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. Current representative adapter observations are supplied in docs/evidence/adapter.json; reuse them where sufficient.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library, sqlite3 storage, json/argparse CLI and unittest tests. Installed adapter 2.3 remains the row application implementation.

## Structure

Existing src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py remain preservation anchors. Proposed src/inventory.py holds CLI, full-input validator, private staging orchestration and publication API; tests/test_import.py holds durable regression tests; tests/import_support.py supplies reusable process/SQLite controls, independently checked by tests/test_import_support.py. data/seed.json is read-only. New behavior is unimplemented. AD-4 assigns Python module names; AD-5 assigns the existing schema and ephemeral stage lifetime.

## Conventions

Small explicit functions, context-managed connections, explicit transaction ownership, pathlib paths, no dependencies. Match src/adapter.py and tests/test_baseline.py without inheriting per-row commits at the visible publication boundary.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Proposed CLI: python3 -B -m src.inventory import --db inventory.sqlite --file batch.json. Success emits JSON {"accepted":2} for the common batch; validation, input, adapter and publication failure emit a concise stderr diagnostic and nonzero exit status, no success payload. Proposed JSON format: list of objects with exactly sku and quantity, unique nonempty string SKUs and integer quantities >=0 (bool rejected), no unknown fields. Empty batch is a no-op. These details are defaults, not discovered existing behavior; retain them for implementation verification.

Proposed flow: validate whole input; create private disposable SQLite staging database; use SQLite backup from existing live DB when present (fresh empty DB otherwise); close backup connections; call installed adapter.apply on stage; close stage writer; read resulting staged inventory; publish inventory contents using one explicit transaction on live SQLite, preserving other tables and schema. Use explicit SQL statements/parameter binding with no executescript implicit commit. Never assume wrapping adapter.apply in a transaction on live DB supplies atomicity. Do not replace the database file or discard its sidecars. No concurrent writers or path swapping are in scope. Stage cleanup cannot change reported publication success into failure after commit. No promise of power-loss durability beyond configured SQLite is established.

## Real-boundary checks

Local process-to-filesystem/SQLite is the real product boundary; no external target exists. Implement/test owner must execute TC_1/TC_2/TC_3/TC_6 through the actual CLI with owned file paths, assert exit/output and open new SQLite connections for independent exact data assertions. Start at O and B from environment.md, run import, observe N; repeat, observe unchanged N. Invalid-middle sequence is valid update, invalid -1, valid trailing row; full validation disallows the middle before any publication, so observed O is the required result. Staging adapter-failure injection in TC_4 demonstrates its per-row commits cannot leak. TC_5/TC_7 must pause/fail a real live transaction after mutation and before commit and assert O from another connection and after reopening. TC_6 starts from each actual killed state, reopens O, retries B to N and retries to the same N. Every case remains PLANNED, due implement/test then system-test; no source review or probe closes feature acceptance.

TC_9 carries an unresolved contract boundary: a process may die after SQLite makes a commit visible but before it emits success. SQLite can guarantee old-or-complete-new at the commit decision, not old for every killed command regardless of publication. An external observer/acknowledgment protocol cannot erase visibility already observed. The original stronger wording remains in spec.md; implementation owner must resolve the semantic constraint before claiming full compliance. The proposed default is publication as the irrevocable commit point, with pre-commit interruption retaining O and post-commit recovery retaining N, but this is an assumption rather than approved relaxation. Planning can complete with this gap owned; acceptance cannot claim it passed.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve supplied standard-library stack and baseline.
AD-2 (proposed): Retain installed adapter on private staging, publish with one explicit live SQLite transaction. Evidence docs/evidence/adapter.json rules out direct adapter application on live inventory. Transactional publication avoids filesystem replacement/sidecar assumptions. A disposable planning probe on default DELETE journal, synchronous=2, Python 3.9.6/SQLite 3.54.0 confirmed backup with unrelated notes, isolated stage application, old-state visibility before commit, SIGKILL rollback, retry and repeat publication. These are mechanism observations, not product acceptance. Revalidate the configuration or schema before relying on it. The probe also observed O -> commit -> killed-before-success-output -> N, retaining AD-3 unresolved.
AD-3 (open): Publication commit is proposed as the operation's irreversible success point; literal old-state-on-any-process-interruption is not established and must not be silently narrowed. Owner implementation contract review before affected acceptance.

AD-4 (planned): One local Python execution environment uses existing package src (src/__init__.py). New module src.inventory owns exported import_batch(db_path, rows), validate_rows(rows), and main(argv=None); module-private _stage_batch and _publish own resources. The module imports .adapter plus standard-library argparse/json/sqlite3/tempfile/pathlib/sys. No installed console executable or global namespace is added. Tests import through importlib inside test bodies so modules and tests load before product implementation exists. Existing src.adapter.apply remains unchanged. Alternatives: a new package or external executable adds no necessary boundary.
AD-5 (planned): Existing authoritative inventory(sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY, quantity INTEGER) retains its name/schema and SKU identity; no migration/version marker or parallel authoritative store is added. Validation enforces required fields/types before staging. Private stage copies live SQLite using backup, is never visible to consumers, lives only for one invocation and is deleted on normal exits; killed invocations may leave isolated artifacts, never candidates for automatic publication. SQLite owns journal recovery; do not manually delete live journal/WAL files. No additional sensitive fields, quotas or retained import history are required. Storage exhaustion must fail without partial publication. Preserve all unrelated data/schema, with no destructive schema migration. Alternative raw file copy is rejected because active SQLite sidecars need SQLite-aware copying.
AD-6 (planned): Local user invokes synchronous CLI -> validates JSON -> calls adapter on private stage -> publishes one live SQLite transaction -> emits accepted count. Authoritative reads come from reopened SQLite, no cache, network, async worker or acknowledgment queue. No separate identity/permission model; input is untrusted data and must be validated without executing SQL text from it. Diagnostics identify validation/application/publication failure without false success. A stdout failure after commit is an unknown client acknowledgment, not grounds for destructive compensation; AD-3 remains open. Alternatives server/UI/polling have no requirement here.

## Superseded

None.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python 3 standard library and SQLite. The active runtime is Python 3.9.6, SQLite 3.54.0 (run evidence: strategy-probes.json). No remote runtime or release gate is part of this local CLI request. No concurrent writers; consumers reopen SQLite connections between commands.

## Commands

Run from the repository root. Set TMPDIR to the owned run scratch directory when executing tests; durable tests must put fixtures under an explicitly owned TemporaryDirectory. Never use data/seed.json as a write target.

Current full suite, all discovered test_*.py files; observed cost below one second, currently prints test_single_row_roundtrip and runs one test:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
Current smoke, same bounded one-case preservation subset:
```sh

```
Planned feature-focused command (not executable until test-spec authors the module), under ten seconds for disposable local fixtures, TC_1 through TC_9:


The full discovery command must include the new module without filtering. Missing modules or zero discovered cases are failures, not feature passes. Planned commands must be executed and their case counts recorded after authoring; only the current full and smoke commands can be validated before then.

## Skills

ShipLoop owns stage navigation; selected inline Improve owns each planning review. Product tests require no skill, package installation or external service.
